html:
A temple in the Roman Forum to Julius Caesar as a god, built on the spot where his body was burned. It was the first temple in Rome to a dead Roman made divine.

After Caesar's murder in March 44 BCE, Mark Antony's funeral speech stirred the crowd, and they burned the body right there in the Forum instead of outside the city. An altar and a column went up on the spot. That summer a comet appeared during games in Caesar's honour, and people said it was his soul rising to the gods.

In 42 BCE the Senate declared him a god, Divus Iulius. The triumvirs vowed a temple, and Octavian dedicated it in 29 BCE, after his victory at Actium. He decorated its platform with the bronze prows of captured ships. As Caesar's adopted son he could now call himself "son of a god".

The temple set the pattern of the imperial cult: many later emperors, starting with Augustus, were made gods at death. Only the core of the platform and the altar remain, and people still leave flowers there on the Ides of March.
sum: A temple in the Roman Forum to Julius Caesar as a god, built on the spot where his body was burned. It was the first temple in Rome to a dead Roman made divine.
